summary.text: Angular momentum is the rotational counterpart of linear momentum, and it has both a size and a direction.
For a spinning object it is proportional to moment of inertia times angular speed, and moment of inertia depends on where the matter sits relative to the axis.
It stays constant when no net external torque acts, which is why bicycles, gyroscopes and hurricane spirals behave as they do.

facts.label: Spin formula
facts.value: Proportional to moment of inertia times angular speed

facts.label: Adds up over parts
facts.value: Total equals the sum of its parts' angular momenta

facts.label: Torque link
facts.value: Torque is its rate of change

items.prompt: A spinning skater pulls her arms tight against her body, with no outside twist on her. What happens to her spin rate?
items.explain: Pulling matter closer to the axis lowers the moment of inertia. The angular momentum is conserved, so the angular speed must rise.

items.prompt: Why does a thrown flying disc hold a steady tilt in flight?

options.label: Spin makes air push it up
Its spin carries a conserved quantity

items.explain: Flying discs owe their useful properties to conservation of angular momentum.

items.prompt: A spinning wheel's angular momentum is seen to change. What must have acted on it from outside?

options.label: A change in its mass only

items.explain: Angular momentum is conserved only when there is no net external torque, and torque is its rate of change.

items.prompt: Two discs have the same mass. One has its matter packed near the axle and the other spread toward the rim. Which is harder to start spinning?

options.label: Neither, equal mass means equal difficulty
The one packed near the axle
The one spread toward the rim

items.explain: Moment of inertia, a measure of rotational inertia, depends on how matter is distributed and not on mass alone.

items.prompt: What does angular momentum depend on that plain linear momentum does not?

options.label: How long the object has been moving
Which point the position is measured from

items.explain: Unlike linear momentum, angular momentum depends on where the origin is chosen, since the particle's position is measured from it.

items.prompt: Which part of Earth's motion carries its spin angular momentum?

options.label: Its daily turn about the polar axis
Its yearly trip around the Sun

items.explain: Spin angular momentum comes from rotation about the body's own center of mass, while orbital comes from revolving around the Sun.
